name: Highway Infrastructure Ltd
title: Highway Infrastructure Ltd - 544477 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Tollway-led infra firm with record INR 1,143 cr order book and FY27 revenue guide of INR 950 cr, but no capacity or capex discipline data, and management evaded margin and Kaza profitability questions.

summary.headline: FY26 consolidated total income rose 25.6% to INR 633.4 crore and PAT 42.0% to INR 31.8 crore, with a record INR 1,143 crore order book.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 633.4 crore (up 25.6% YoY), EBITDA of INR 51.5 crore (up 28.4%) and PAT of INR 31.8 crore (up 42.0%), with debt-to-equity at 0.45x and ROE at 18.4%. The closing order book was a record INR 1,143 crore, and the company won the Kaza Fee Plaza toll contract (about INR 328.8 crore), the largest in its history. Management said it walked away from two toll projects (Venkatapalam penalty of INR 26.33 lakh; Katiyara handed over) on commercial grounds. Most of the call focused on the wayside amenities and ropeway opportunities, and on FY27 revenue guidance of INR 950 crore.

segments.name: Tollway collection
segments.commentary: Contributed 73.7% of FY26 revenue; Kaza Fee Plaza (Andhra Pradesh, about INR 328.8 crore) is the largest toll contract won. Stated segment margin is about 7%. Toll order book balance was INR 526.1 crore as of March 2026.

segments.name: EPC infrastructure
segments.commentary: Contributed 19.8% of FY26 revenue; 105+ completed and 30+ ongoing projects. Balance EPC works INR 591.3 crore as of March 2026; stated margin 13-14% with a floor of about 13-14% GP. Order book is currently dominated by Madhya Pradesh.

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.5% of FY26 revenue; revenue rose to INR 41.6 crore from INR 8.0 crore in FY25. Management cited margins of about 50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR 950 crore: EPC about INR 300 crore and Toll about INR 650 crore (stated in Q&A).

Order book conversion: about INR 200 crore of the INR 600 crore FY26 addition expected to execute in FY27 (33.3%); toll book fully executed within the year. Earlier, FY27 was framed as INR 900 crore (EPC 200, toll 700) and FY28 as INR 1,200 crore (EPC 300, toll 900), which do not match the later INR 950 crore figure.
Wayside amenities break-even estimated at 5-8 years on a 30-year contract and 3-5 (maybe 7) years on a 20-year contract; cash outlay not quantified.
Margin improvement levers under review, but management declined to quantify a FY27 margin target and said benefits will not necessarily come within one year.
Government allocated INR 3.1 lakh crore to MoRTH for FY27.
capex_capacity: Wayside amenities (NHLML/NHAI PPP model): company says it has been bidding on controlled-access corridors; cash outflow not disclosed. Government reports 501 awarded and 94 operational as of April 2025, with more than 700 expected by FY29.
Ropeway (Parvatmala) opportunities under evaluation as an EPC and operations play; no quantified plan given.
Renewable/EV charging EPC: two EV charging projects commissioned in Indore; more being scoped.
Management said the balance sheet can support wayside capex, with timing and funding (debt or equity) to be decided later.
Geographic footprint: presence in 11 states and 1 Union Territory; Northeast being evaluated for toll and EPC work.
demand_pricing: EPC bid pipeline INR 300-400 crore; win rate approximately 20-25%.
EPC policy: will not go below about 13-14% gross profit; industry peers may bid below 10%.
Toll: company says traffic grows 5-7% annually (up to 10% on some corridors). MLFF rollout seen as limited near-term impact; management views it as positive for PPP-based operators.
Toll strategy is pan-India and not concentrated in one region; regions cited as strong include Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Delhi-NCR and Uttar Pradesh.
Two toll projects were declined or exited on commercial grounds: Venkatapalam (withdrawn, penalty INR 26.33 lakh) and Katiyara (handed over, Bihar).

qa_highlights.question: How does HIL differentiate itself in winning large EPC and toll contracts while protecting profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited pan-India toll coverage, in-house technology for revenue monitoring and leakage control, and an EPC floor of about 13-14% GP, with selective bidding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the potential impact of MLFF tolling on the toll business and how will it be mitigated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views MLFF as positive: it is PPP-based, lowers operator risk, lengthens tenure and reduces competition; no mitigation planned as it sees no issue. Company is studying MLFF opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How will the order book convert to revenue in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO-level answer gave FY27 at INR 900 crore (EPC 200, toll 700) and FY28 at INR 1,200 crore (EPC 300, toll 900). Later, FY27 was stated as INR 950 crore (EPC about 300, toll 650).

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of wayside amenities, including cash outgo, break-even and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash outflow not quantified; break-even 5-8 years on 30-year and about 3-7 years on 20-year contracts; balance sheet said to be supportive, with timing undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about INR 65 crore, of which INR 27 crore was billed in March and is realisable within three months; management called it a timing issue, to clear within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EPC pipeline, win rate and FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline INR 300-400 crore with 20-25% win rate; FY27 guidance INR 950 crore (EPC about 300, toll about 650).

qa_highlights.question: Can margins improve above the FY26 level of about 8% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; cited software-driven reductions in site manpower and leakage. Said improvements are a longer-term, continuous process.

risks_watch: Inconsistent FY27 revenue figures in the call (INR 900 crore vs INR 950 crore) and FY28 INR 1,200 crore; confirm against the investor presentation.
Segment margins: toll about 7% against EPC 13-14%; a mix shift toward toll may dilute consolidated margins. FY26 margin cited at about 8%.
Wayside and ropeway entry: cash outlay, funding and returns are unquantified; management declined to give revenue ranges.
EPC pipeline concentration in Madhya Pradesh; win rate of 20-25% on INR 300-400 crore pipeline.
Receivables rise, with about INR 65 crore outstanding and INR 27 crore billed in March; monitor collection within six months.
Limited near-term effect of MLFF assumed by management; the transition timeline and corridor selection are uncertain.
Kaza Fee Plaza profitability not disclosed on the call; management referred queries to a one-on-one follow-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order book, but cautious and evasive on specifics: management declined to quantify wayside cash outlay, ropeway revenue, Kaza profitability and the FY27 margin target, citing subjectivity.
key_quotes: We closed the year with the highest -ever order book of over INR 1,000 crores.
We are not pursuing scale for its own sake, nor are we prepared to compromise on project economics simply to expand the order book.
We will remain selective, focused on return thresholds, margin quality, and long-term value creation, and we will continue to walk away from opportunities that do not meet our internal standards.
